as_told.title: The Space Act lets NASA withhold sensitive findings

plain: The National Aeronautics and Space Act, the law Congress passed in 1958 to create NASA, is said to bind the space agency closely to the Department of Defense and let it keep certain findings secret. If that is so, anything sensitive NASA found could stay hidden. Maaneli Derakhshani, a guest on the podcast, makes the basic point, saying NASA and the Defense Department "have always been very tightly linked in law" through that act. Michels goes further in his own narration of a separate episode. He says findings judged "outside the civilian mandate" could be held back. In practice, he says, that meant a breakthrough in propulsion, a powerful new sensor, "or even contact with non-human intelligence" could be "withheld indefinitely." Both describe the law in their own words rather than quoting its text.
